explanation: The name used for God in the Old Testament, referring to his authority and power.
An agreement or promise between God and people, especially with the nation of Israel.
The term for the descendants of Jacob (also called Israel), who make up the twelve tribes of ancient Israel.
The land where the children of Israel were slaves under the Egyptian pharaoh.
The prophet and leader whom God chose to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt and into the promised land.
Moses' brother and spokesman, who helped him confront Pharaoh and lead the children of Israel out of Egypt.
The Egyptian king who held the children of Israel as slaves and refused to let them go.
The ten disasters that God sent upon Egypt to punish Pharaoh and his people, and to make them release the children of Israel.
The region that God promised to give to the children of Israel as their homeland, also known as Canaan.
The term used to describe God's action of destroying enemies or evil forces.
